scenario: Replace PermG observed FPR=0% with hypothetical FPR=10%

k3_majority_voting.mechanism: Equal-weight majority voting (K>=3 of 5 methods agree)
k3_majority_voting.reason: Each method contributes exactly 1 vote regardless of FPR. Changing FPR assumption does not change vote counts.
k3_majority_voting.conclusion: K>=3 consensus results are IDENTICAL under both assumptions.

key_arguments: Even at FPR=10%, PermG remains the lowest-FPR method (next: TY at 16.7%, DiffXCorr at 37.5%).
Main results use equal-weight K>=3 voting, completely unaffected by FPR magnitude.
FPR-inverse weighting is exploratory only; PermG weight drops from infinity to 10 but remains highest (TY=6.0, Threshold=4.0, DiffXCorr=2.67, Naive=1.09).
Rank order is preserved: PermG remains #1 position.
Robustness conclusion: the MMCT framework is insensitive to PermG FPR assumptions because (a) majority voting is equal-weight, and (b) even with 10% FPR, PermG dominates all alternatives.
conclusion: PermG remains optimal under FPR=10% hypothesis. K>=3 voting unaffected (equal-weight). FPR-inverse ranking preserved (PermG still #1). Framework is robust to this sensitivity assumption.
